references.text: The Lord commanded Moses to teach the people laws and statutes, which corresponds to the task of presenting ordinances to the Israelites.
Moses receives the command to teach the people commands, laws, and statutes, paralleling the formulation about presenting the ordinances to them.
Moses proclaimed all the words of the Lord and all the laws to the people, which is a direct follow-up to the command in 21:1.
The Levites shall teach Jacob your statutes and Israel your law, which relates to the transmission of mishpatim (ordinances).
God declared his words, laws, and commands to Jacob and Israel, reflecting the same tradition of presenting God's ordinances.
At Mara, the Lord gave the people law and justice (חֹק וּמִשְׁפָּט), preparing for the additional mishpatim in chapter 21.
The Lord's statutes and laws are to be kept, referring to the same type of ordinances presented from Exodus 21.
Both verses illustrate the prophetic and educational task of conveying God's statutes as a living way for the people.
